decision: Owner 2026-09-22: proceed with the lead's recommendations on the held decisions. hydraulics beginner hb_tau_y_Pa: RE-KEY (found by W4a, README 'W4a' known coincidences).

why: hb_tau_y_Pa graded the capstone mud's Herschel-Bulkley yield stress, (2 x 5 - 6) = 4 dial degrees = 2.04161424376 Pa. The light mud (light_wbm) reads 4 degrees at 3 rpm, so the rheology explorer's default Three models view on either light_wbm case printed that exact stress in its residual table (Measured, theta3 row) with the Your mud boxes blank.

Keeping the quantity would need a new capstone mud, which moves all eighteen fields on three tiers. Re-keyed instead onto the Herschel-Bulkley flow behaviour index n of the same capstone mud: it is fitted after the yield stress is taken off the 600 and 300 rpm stresses, so the yield rule is still worked (the Bingham yield point there gives n = 1), and it prints only when the mud is typed into the Your mud boxes (Tile 'Herschel-Bulkley n', 8 dp). The tolerance is pl_n's, 5e-7, which the 8 dp print carries with room to spare.
prompt_edits: (1) the POWER LAW flow behaviour index n for that mud, which is not the Herschel-Bulkley n; (2) the HERSCHEL-BULKLEY yield stress in pascals, which is not the Bingham yield point and is less than half of it;

(1) the POWER LAW flow behaviour index n for that mud, from the 600 and 300 rpm readings alone; (2) the HERSCHEL-BULKLEY flow behaviour index n, fitted to the 600 and 300 rpm stresses once the Herschel-Bulkley yield stress from the 6 and 3 rpm readings is taken off both, which is larger than field 1;
